query: What concrete anomaly-detection thresholds, FP/FN tradeoffs, tuning guidance, and expected alert volumes should telemetry triggers use at pilot scale?

response.query: What concrete anomaly-detection thresholds, FP/FN tradeoffs, tuning guidance, and expected alert volumes should telemetry triggers use at pilot scale?
response.answer: For pilot scale, anomaly detection thresholds should balance sensitivity and specificity to minimize false positives and negatives, with expected alert volumes based on historical data trends. Adjust thresholds for response time, failure rates, and load changes to suit specific service or application needs. Use fixed or adaptive thresholds based on observed performance patterns.

results.title: Understanding TP, FP, FN, and TN in Cybersecurity | by Vineeth Tunk | Medium
results.content: Peter triggers alerts — but is it real? ### ❌ False Positive (FP) — “Oops… blocked a harmless Peter.” ### ❌ False Negative (FN) — “You missed it!” Every detection tool in security tries to get this balance right — and when it fails, Peter either gets blocked unfairly… or breaks your site 😅 Miss one real attack (FN), and it’s not just downtime — it’s data, trust, and dollars lost. *Not Today, Hacker* is a storytelling-style blog series where I break down web app security using real-world examples, memes, and the occasional disaster starring **Peter Griffin**. **Let’s clear the confusion — one alert, one Peter, and one detection matrix at a time.

results.title: Anomaly detection | New Relic Documentation
results.content: Anomaly detection gives your team the ability to alert on any entity or signal and to adjust and optimize your sensitivity thresholds. Anomaly detection uses the same streaming-alerting pipeline as static threshold alerts and shares the same advanced tuning settings. You can create anomaly sensitivity thresholds from an alert condition. The threshold value for anomaly detection controls the sensitivity of the alert condition for tolerating how far off the actual value is from the predicted value. The threshold is the number of standard deviations your signal value is away from the value that was predicted. Selecting **for at least** means that ALL of your signal's data points must be outside of the threshold for the specified time period before an incident is opened. The **at least once in** option simply means that as soon as any of your signal's data points are outside of the threshold, an incident will open. All of your signal's data points must be within the threshold for the specified period of time. Think of this as how long the signal value must remain outside the threshold before an incident is opened. Conversely, it's also how long a signal must be within the threshold for an incident to be closed. For custom anomaly detection, this is the number of standard deviations the signal's data point is from the value that we predicted it would be. ## Setting thresholds for multi-signal conditions (faceted queries). The threshold settings that you specify apply the same to all signals being monitored by this condition. But, we don't show the predicted signal and threshold bands when there is more than one signal shown on the chart. * **Consistency of data** For metric values that remain in a consistent range or that trend slowly and steadily, their more predictable behavior means that their sensitivity thresholds will become tighter around the prediction. By default, anomaly detection automatically calculates each signal's seasonality using **New Relic calculation**. * **Hourly**: Applies an hourly pattern to all signals within the condition for anomaly detection. * **Daily**: Applies a daily pattern to all signals within the condition for anomaly detection. * **Weekly**: Applies a weekly pattern to all signals within the condition for anomaly detection.

results.title: Adjust the sensitivity of anomaly detection for services — Dynatrace Docs
results.content: Dynatrace detects four types of anomalies for services: **response time degradations**, **increases in failure rate**, **service load drops**, and **service load spikes**. This type of anomaly detection observes the response time of your services and triggers an alert if a metric violates the specified thresholds. 1. Turn on **Detect response time degradation** and select **using fixed thresholds** from the list. This type of anomaly detection observes the failure rate of your services and triggers an alert if the rate exceeds the specified thresholds. This type of anomaly detection learns the normal behavior of your service load over a period of 7 days and triggers an alert if the load drops significantly. This type of anomaly detection learns the normal behavior of your service load over a period of 7 days and triggers an alert if the load increases significantly. * To set lower response-time thresholds for specific, business-critical service requests. * To set higher response-time thresholds for volatile service requests that are non-business critical.

results.title: Adjust the sensitivity of anomaly detection for applications — Dynatrace Docs
results.content: Dynatrace detects four types of anomalies for applications: **key performance metric degradations**, **traffic drops**, **traffic spikes**, and **increases in failure rate**. This type of anomaly detection observes key performance metrics and triggers an alert if a metric violates the specified threshold. 1. Turn on **Detect key performance metric time degradations** and select **using fixed thresholds** from the list. This type of anomaly detection learns the normal behavior of your application's traffic over a period of 7 days and triggers an alert if the traffic drops significantly. This type of anomaly detection learns the normal behavior of your application's traffic over a period of 7 days and triggers an alert if the traffic rises significantly. This type of anomaly detection observes the failure rate of your applications and triggers an alert if the rate exceeds the specified thresholds. Dynatrace can detect failure rate increase based on automatic baselining or fixed thresholds. 1. Turn on **Detect increase in failure rate** and select **using fixed thresholds** from the list.
